summary: Candidate B implements the frozen contract directly and with disciplined scope; Candidate A violates explicit requirements by duplicating Add and changing global request/retry behavior.
reasons: B validates inputs, uses internal/multipartbody.NewFile("file", fileName, content), and delegates directly to s.Add(ctx, body, contentType, opts...), preserving established option, response, and error handling.
B’s tests cover multipart field, filename, content, replay of streamed content after a 429, pre-request validation, and source-reader failure.
A does not route Upload through FilesService.Add; it duplicates Add’s option processing, request construction, response decoding, and missing-data error path.

A changes RawClient.Do to buffer nearly every non-native io.Reader, altering Files.Add, Files.Update, and unrelated SDK requests despite the contract explicitly requiring Add behavior to remain unchanged and forbidding unrelated retry refactoring.
risks_a: Global buffering can introduce unexpected memory use, source-reader errors before any request, and behavior changes across unrelated APIs.
The duplicated Upload implementation can drift from Add as option or error semantics evolve.
Documentation advertises behavior changes outside the requested convenience API.
risks_b: The retry test validates multipart content only on the retried request rather than asserting identical complete bodies on both attempts.
The new Upload test does not explicitly exercise FilesOption forwarding, though delegation to the existing Add method makes that behavior straightforward.
